focus: ADR-0007 MCP 2026-07-28 vs 2025 clients; client identity when clientInfo comes only at initialize

findings.title: ADR-0007 decision 4 (stateless, identity never from the connection) breaks the #542/#539 clientInfo-based platform detection that ctx_upgrade and ctx_doctor rely on for 2025-xx clients
findings.claim: ADR-0007 decision 4 says the server keeps no per-connection state and identifies the client only from request _meta and hook payloads, 'never from the connection.' This rule is written for both the 2026-07-28 clients (where _meta on every request carries protocol version and client capabilities) and the 2025-xx clients the server still serves. But the 2025-xx MCP handshake sends clientInfo only once, in the initialize request. It is not repeated in the _meta of later requests (confirmed by ADR-0007's own quote of the 2026-07-28 changelog, which says the 'every request carries its _meta' behaviour is new in that version). So for a 2025-xx client, the only place clientInfo exists is the initialize call that the SDK answers when it opens the connection; reading it at tool-call time, as v1 does, is reading state tied to the connection.
findings.evidence: v1 fixed issue #542 (Pi/OMP misdetected as Cursor) and #539 (Claude Code misdetected inside VS Code) by capturing clientInfo in-process at tool-call time via `server.server.getClientVersion()` and trusting it over every other signal. Commit 7e67952c 'fix(detect): thread MCP clientInfo through ctx_upgrade to upgrade() (closes #542 partial - 3 of 6)', src/server.ts: 'Capture the live MCP clientInfo via server.server.getClientVersion() (in-process - no spawn boundary loses the handshake info)'. Commit 8b9d13a1 'test(detect): pin MCP clientInfo priority over env-var detection (closes #539 partial - 4 of 5)' pins that detect.ts:135 must prefer clientInfo.name over every env var, including a polluted-shell case. `getClientVersion()` in the MCP SDK returns the clientInfo captured by the SDK at initialize and held on the connection object - exactly the per-connection state ADR-0007 decision 4 forbids reading. docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md 3.11 rewrites ctx_upgrade for v2 as 'Read the install mode from the adapter table' and drops any mention of clientInfo or a --platform flag threaded from the MCP handler; it does not say how, under decision 4's rule, a 2025-xx tool call recovers the clientInfo.name signal #542 and #539 were fixed on.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: 7e67952c (2026-05-12) 'fix(detect): thread MCP clientInfo through ctx_upgrade to upgrade() (closes #542 partial - 3 of 6)', and 8b9d13a1 (2026-05-12) 'test(detect): pin MCP clientInfo priority over env-var detection (closes #539 partial - 4 of 5)', both in cm-main. ORIGINAL_INTENT (quoted from 7e67952c): 'Captures the live MCP clientInfo via server.server.getClientVersion() (in-process - no spawn boundary loses the handshake info). Resolves the PlatformId via detectPlatform(clientInfo). ... short-circuits the heuristic chain.' and from 8b9d13a1: 'when the MCP initialize handshake supplies clientInfo.name, the client-map lookup wins over any env-var permutation.' REGRESSION_RISK: if v2's ctx_upgrade/ctx_doctor literally follow ADR-0007 decision 4 and never read clientInfo off the connection for 2025-xx clients, the highest-confidence platform signal from #542/#539 is unavailable at tool-call time, and detection falls back to the env-var/config-dir heuristics those two issues were filed against (Pi/OMP vs Cursor collision, Claude-Code-in-VS-Code collision) - a direct re-break of two closed issues. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: ADR-0007 should say explicitly, for 2025-xx clients, that the SDK's own initialize-time clientInfo cache is the one exception allowed to decision 4 (it is handshake data, not session/user state, and GP1/GP2 already test it per protocolVersion), or it should specify a replacement for the #542/#539 signal that does not depend on reading the connection - e.g. requiring 2025-xx clients' every tool call to pass clientInfo again in a tool argument, which no current client does and the live probe (2026-10-14) did not observe.
findings.fix: In ADR-0007, add a line under decision 4 that scopes 'never from the connection' to session/user identity, and explicitly allow reading the SDK's cached initialize clientInfo for platform/adapter detection in ctx_doctor and ctx_upgrade when serving a 2025-xx client. Add a GP1/GP2 case that runs ctx_upgrade under a 2025-xx initialize handshake with a Pi clientInfo and asserts the #542 fix still resolves PiAdapter, so the ADR's stated test plan actually covers this path.

findings.title: ADR-0007 does not say what identifies the client for 2026-07-28's own stateless server/discover path once no initialize ever ran
findings.claim: Decision 4 says identity comes from request _meta and hook payloads for the stateless 2026-07-28 flow. ADR-0007's own live probe table shows neither Claude Code 2.1.283 nor Codex CLI 0.156.1 calls server/discover today - both still call initialize. So the ADR's stated identity mechanism for 2026-07-28 ('_meta on every request') is untested against any real client; GP1/GP2 only test it with a synthetic stateless client built for the test.
findings.evidence: ADR-0007 table: 'Claude Code 2.1.283 | initialize | 2025-11-25' and 'Codex CLI 0.156.1 | initialize | 2025-06-18'. 'Neither client called server/discover.' Test section: 'GP-LIVE runs the real agents and logs the protocol version each one negotiated, so a version change in an agent shows up' - this only logs the version, it does not say GP-LIVE checks client identity resolution for a real stateless caller, because none exists yet.
findings.archaeology: No v1 precedent exists for server/discover or for an identity read purely off per-request _meta, since v1 only ever served initialize-based clients; this is new code with no prior issue history, so archaeology does not apply beyond confirming (via the same git log search used for finding 1) that no file in cm-main implements or tests a _meta-only identity path.
findings.fix: State in ADR-0007 that the _meta-based identity path is currently untested against any production client and is covered only by the synthetic GP1/GP2 harness; add a follow-up item to re-test once a real 2026-07-28 client ships, rather than implying GP-LIVE already covers this case.
